clue.text: Operated radio show in Burma

definitions.note: a definition by location: a place in Burma, here its former capital city

parts.note: operated, as in ran a business, gives the past tense RAN
The Goon Show was a famous BBC radio comedy series, so a radio show gives GOON

explanation.surface: Someone who ran a radio programme while stationed in Burma.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a classic 1950s BBC radio comedy starring Spike Milligan and Peter Sellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon, now Yangon, was the capital city of Burma, so it is a place found in that country.

clue.text: Communist and German worker sacked ?

parts.note: a red is a Communist
und is the German word for and
an ant is the typical worker in crossword clues

explanation.surface: A Communist and a German labourer have both lost their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made redundant is losing one's job because it is no longer needed, a form of dismissal.

clue.text: Offensive number is nothing to me

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An offensive musical number means nothing to me.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul-smelling or disgusting, hence objectionable.

clue.text: Is. putting on too much weight !

definitions.text: Is. putting on too much weight

parts.words: Is. putting on too much weight
parts.note: reads as someone getting fat, but means loading a vehicle or structure beyond its capacity

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is getting too fat.
explanation.definitionFit: To overload is to place more burden on something than it can safely carry.

clue.text: Curious wares, her grand, grandfather's

parts.note: points to the Dickens heroine whose grandfather kept The Old Curiosity Shop, full of strange goods

explanation.surface: A girl's grandfather owns odd merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop, the little heroine lives with her grandfather among his curios.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Nell is the Dickens heroine whose grandfather runs The Old Curiosity Shop.

clue.text: No mixed bathing in these hills ?

definitions.text: No mixed bathing in these hills ?

parts.words: No mixed bathing in these hills ?
parts.note: if only one sex may bathe in these hills, it is the men who take a dip, and that phrase run together names a range of English hills

explanation.surface: A notice of single-sex swimming rules in some hill country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mendip Hills are a limestone range in Somerset, south-west England; split the name as MEN DIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mendips are a range of limestone hills in Somerset, whose name splits as men taking a dip.

clue.text: Keep to oneself in some pool perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters are only one possible arrangement, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A swimmer who hogs a public pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the ten letters of IN SOME POOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To monopolise is to keep sole possession or control of something.

clue.text: There's not any point in a date in Rome

parts.note: none means not any
S is a point of the compass, south

explanation.surface: Someone claims a date in Rome has no point.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman calendar fixed dates by the Kalends, Nones and Ides; the Nones fell on the 5th or 7th of a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nones was a fixed day of the ancient Roman month, used for reckoning dates.

clue.text: Working as a member of the brotherhood

definitions.meaning: functioning properly, as a machine in good working condition

definitions.text: as a member of the brotherhood
definitions.meaning: belonging to a monastic or religious fraternity

explanation.surface: A monk who has a job within his fraternity.
explanation.definitionFit: In order means functioning correctly, and one in a religious order belongs to that brotherhood.

clue.text: How put on this extra attraction for teams ?

definitions.text: How put on this extra attraction for teams ?

parts.words: How put on this extra attraction for teams ?
parts.note: the word how added after the word for teams gives a lesser attraction at a fair, beside the main show

explanation.surface: A question about staging a bonus event for competing squads.
explanation.walkthrough: Teams are sides; put HOW on SIDES and you get SIDESHOW, an extra attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Teams opposing each other in a game are the two sides.

clue.text: Forcible method of gaining entrance

parts.note: reads like breaking in by force, but a forcible push is one sense of the word, and a private road up to a house is the way in

explanation.surface: A burglar's technique for breaking into a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a forceful push or thrust, and also the private road by which one reaches a house.

clue.text: Mouldy work by laundress ?

parts.note: mouldy here means made of carved mouldings, and a laundress's work is folding sheets and tablecloths, which together suggest a carved panel pattern

explanation.surface: A washerwoman's work gone mildewed and rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouldy' suggests mildew but means 'of mouldings': linenfold is carved wooden panelling made to look like folded cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Linenfold is a style of carved wooden panelling moulded to imitate folded cloth, the kind a laundress might fold.

clue.text: The silly chap's in the soup

definitions.meaning: old slang for a fool or simpleton
something found in soup, the strips of pasta in a broth

explanation.surface: A foolish man has landed himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' is an idiom for being in trouble, but here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is dated slang for a simpleton, and noodles are pasta strips served in broth.

clue.text: Makers of serials, to vary these, despise nothing

indicators.note: to vary these letters is to change their order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Advice that those producing serials should change things, despising nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to vary' tells you to rearrange DESPISE plus O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: A serial is made up of instalments, so its instalments are what make it.

clue.text: Conventional representation of hi-fi lover

definitions.meaning: a fixed, oversimplified image of a kind of person
a person devoted to sound systems, a type keen on stereo equipment

explanation.surface: A clichéd portrait of an audio enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is a fixed, oversimplified image, and split it describes the sort of person keen on stereo systems.

clue.text: Literary lone wolf has a lake-upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters of lake are jumbled

explanation.surface: A famous wolf from a book has knocked over a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges LAKE into AKEL, then A, given as it is, goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela is the wise old wolf who leads the pack in Kipling's Jungle Book, hence a wolf from literature.

clue.text: Tournament sites that are far from level?

definitions.meaning: arenas where knights jousted at medieval tournaments
pieces of ground set on a slant, tilted enclosures

explanation.surface: Jousting grounds that turn out to be lopsided.
explanation.walkthrough: Tilting is jousting with lances; read the other way, tilted yards would slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiltyards were enclosures for jousting, called tilting, and taken as tilted yards they would slope badly.

clue.text: At US university long hair can prevent unwanted admission

parts.note: Yale is an Ivy League university in Connecticut
locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A long-haired student at an American college keeps out intruders.
explanation.walkthrough: Yale locks are cylinder door locks named after their inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale locks are cylinder door fastenings that stop intruders entering.

clue.text: Rock gives 'the sea-shore character

parts.note: the sands are a beach, the sea-shore
tone means character or quality, as in the tone of a place

explanation.surface: A rock gives the beach its distinctive feel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock made of compacted sand grains.

clue.text: What on earth can moth or rust damage?

definitions.text: What on earth can moth or rust damage?

parts.words: What on earth can moth or rust damage?
parts.note: echoes the Sermon on the Mount warning not to lay up riches on earth, where moth and rust corrupt

explanation.surface: An exasperated question about what harm moths or rust could possibly do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What on earth' sounds like exasperation, but it is literal: Matthew 6:19 speaks of earthly valuables 'where moth and rust doth corrupt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew's Gospel names earthly riches as what moth and rust destroy.

clue.text: Turn out on football team

parts.note: to evert is to turn inside out

explanation.surface: Fans turn out to support a football team.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Premier League club from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Liverpool club in English professional football.

clue.text: Get to know the river navy

parts.note: the Lea is a river flowing through north-east London
RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A recruit getting acquainted with the river navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to come to know it.

clue.text: Scarface leaves commonwealth for a republic

indicators.note: leaves means departs from, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: the official name of the country is the Commonwealth of Australia
Scarface was the nickname of gangster Al Capone, giving AL

explanation.surface: A scarred man emigrates from a dominion to a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes AL from AUSTRALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a central European federal state with an elected president.

clue.text: Dislike a translation

parts.note: a version is a rendering of a text in another language

explanation.surface: Someone takes against a particular translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion is a strong distaste for something.

clue.text: Bikini-one Lolita lost perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the remaining letters are one of many possible orders, so they are rearranged
lost means gone missing, so that letter drops out of the girl's name

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Lolita character loses her bikini.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes I (one) from LOLITA; 'perhaps' rearranges LOLTA. Bikini is the Pacific coral island, not the swimsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is an example of a coral reef island in the Marshall Islands, used for nuclear tests.

clue.text: Point to high class art arising from Sanskrit maxims

definitions.note: plural maxims define a singular word meaning a collection of such aphorisms

parts.note: S is a point of the compass, south
U is the British label for upper-class speech and manners

indicators.note: arising means coming up, which in a down entry reads the word art from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Aphorisms in Sanskrit point towards refined art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns ART to TRA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutra is a collection of short aphoristic rules in Sanskrit literature.

clue.text: Surgeon, about to continue, blows up

indicators.note: about means going round, so the surgeon's letters wrap around the next piece

parts.note: BS is the abbreviation for Bachelor of Surgery, a surgeon's degree
to last is to go on or continue

explanation.surface: A surgeon, on the point of carrying on, loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts BS around LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasts and blows up both mean destroys with explosions.

clue.text: Where some manufactured a modern cheese

indicators.note: some of the following words signals that part of their run of letters is the answer

explanation.surface: Where certain producers made a contemporary cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points into manufacturED A Modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese sold in balls coated in red wax.

clue.text: How a runner beat his rivals but lost his welcome

definitions.text: How a runner beat his rivals
definitions.meaning: by having more stamina than the others over the distance
remained so long as guest that he was no longer wanted

explanation.surface: A racer won through stamina but then stayed too long at the party.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay rivals is to last longer than them, and a guest who stays too long has worn out his hosts' hospitality.

clue.text: Bar on union by writer Rolfe

definitions.text: Bar on union by writer Rolfe

parts.words: Bar on union by writer Rolfe
parts.note: join the words bar and on into one title, and that title goes with the pen name Frederick Rolfe used

explanation.surface: A writer named Rolfe imposes a ban on a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederick Rolfe, author of Hadrian the Seventh, styled himself Baron Corvo; 'Bar on' united is the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Rolfe published under the self-styled title and pseudonym Baron Corvo.

clue.text: A connexion with the days before headlights

definitions.meaning: a joining or bond between things
the era when a torch carrier, called a link, lit the way through dark streets, read as a period of history

explanation.surface: A link with the era before cars had lamps.
explanation.walkthrough: A link was a pitch torch carried by a linkboy to light pedestrians at night; connexion is an old spelling of connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A linkage is a connection, and read in two parts it is the age of the torch called a link.

clue.text: Mother's wise at physiotherapy

parts.note: Ma is mother, so mother's is MA'S
sage means wise

explanation.surface: Mum is skilled at physiotherapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Massage, rubbing and kneading of muscles, is a standard physiotherapy treatment.
